The heavy doors swing shut on golden dust,
No whisper left among the stacked-up spines.
The clock has stopped its tick; all trust
In quiet worlds now ends in final signs.

The sun dips low behind the window pane.
We lose our minds within these wooden boxes,
And leave them empty, dry, and plain.
The shadows stretch across the reading room,
Where eyes once scanned the pages, bright and deep.
Now darkness falls like any other gloom,
Promises kept, but secrets buried sleep.
So close the book; the story finds its end,
No voice remains for us to comprehend.
